title: Hyperlipidemia/Hypertriglyceridemia
desc: Low-fat diet, Chitin / chitosan fibre, Omega-3 fatty acids, Bezafibrate
notes: Diet change- low fat. Recheck fasting triglycerides after 1 month (goal is < 500)
Chitin or Chitosan fiber supplement. 250 to 500 mg BID
Bezafibrate 4-10 mg/kg SID (Fiona Stocker on 100 mg SID, 40 lb dog)
Most clinical signs occur when triglycerides are >500 mg/dL (>5.65 mmol/L) but there are many patients who do not have clinical signs
even when the value is > 1,000 mg/dL (>11.3 mmol/L). Generally speaking, if the initial result was not on a fasted sample, a value >500 mg/dL (>5.65 mmol/L)
should be rechecked on a fasted sample and if still > 500 mg/dL (>5.65 mmol/L), underlying reasons for the elevated value should be explored.
Ocular changes such as lipid keratopathy, arcus lipoides,
stromal dystrophy, lipid in the aqueous humor, uveitis, blindness, and lipemia retinalis.
Dermatological manifestations such as cutaneous xanthomata, pruritus, and alopecia.
Xanthomas may also be seen in organs (liver, spleen, kidney, heart, skeletal muscle and intestine).
Central nervous system disturbances such as seizures, behavioral changes, neuropathies,
and cerebral atherosclerosis. These signs do not usually occur until the triglycerides exceed 1000 mg/dL.
